tagline: Turn a text-based PDF's tables into an Excel workbook — on your device, nothing uploaded.
description:
PDF Tables → Excel pulls the tables out of a born-digital PDF and hands you back a real .xlsx — one sheet per page — entirely on your own device. Nothing is ever uploaded.

It was built for SERFF insurance rate and rule filings, which are almost always born-digital (exported from actuarial software). That means the numbers are real text with real positions, so the tool reconstructs the row-and-column grid EXACTLY — no OCR, no guessing. It reads the PDF with pdf.js, clusters the text into rows (by vertical position) and columns (by the left-edges that recur down the page), and writes the workbook with SheetJS.

HONEST ABOUT LIMITS. A scanned (image-only) PDF has no text to read — the tool says so plainly rather than handing you an empty sheet. And it reconstructs aligned grids, not merged or nested cells. For the rate tables SERFF exports, that is exactly the shape.

Everything runs sealed in the app sandbox with no network access at all: the PDF you drop in, and the Excel file that comes out, never leave this browser.
author: GifOS
